standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the statement meaningful by showing a finite type sheaf on a locally Noetherian scheme is coherent and that flat pullback preserves this, and supplies the final equality relating length_B(B tensor_A M) to length_A(M) times length_B(B/m_A B).

core_obligations: Settle the dimension statements and reduce part (1) to part (2): the dimension bounds follow at once from the inverse image dimension lemma, and part (1) follows from part (2) because the pullback of the structure sheaf of Z is the structure sheaf of the preimage of Z, with the cycle classes of subschemes and structure sheaves identified (proof lines 2351-2355).

Make the statement meaningful: on a locally Noetherian scheme a finite type sheaf is coherent, so F is coherent and its flat pullback is again coherent, which the coherence lemma and the pullback of finite type sheaves give (proof lines 2357-2364).

Compare the two coefficients: for an integral W of delta-dimension k and an integral W' of dimension k + r mapping into it, with generic points xi and xi', let A, B be the local rings and M the stalk of F; then the coefficient in the flat pullback of the sheaf class is length_B(B tensor_A M) while the coefficient in the pulled back cycle class is length_A(M) times length_B(B/m_A B), and the equality follows from the flat pullback formula for lengths (proof lines 2365-2387).
proof_roadmap: Dimension bounds and the reduction of part (1) to part (2) (proof lines 2351-2355).
Coherence of the sheaf and of its pullback on a locally Noetherian scheme (proof lines 2357-2364).
Coefficient comparison at the generic points of a component and its preimage components (proof lines 2365-2387).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the flat pullback of the cycle class of a closed subscheme and of a coherent sheaf: the support dimension grows by the relative dimension and the class of the pullback is the pullback of the class (statement lines 2330-2349, tag 02RE). The dimension statements are immediate from the inverse image dimension lemma, but the class comparison requires a real local computation: after checking that the pulled back sheaf is coherent on a locally Noetherian scheme, one compares at the generic points of an integral component of the target and of a component of its preimage, where the two coefficients are length_B(B tensor_A M) and length_A(M) length_B(B/m_A B), and identifies them by the flat pullback formula for lengths. That coefficient comparison is the substance, so the claim is H2.
